prompt:
You hold 50 long adjusted GE1 calls with strike 14.00 and premium quote 0.25. Hypothetical expiry GE share price after cash-in-lieu fixing is 120.00. Reconcile the initial reverse-split notice, August 6 expiration-pricing notice and August 18 fixed-cash notice. Compare the provisional pricing formula at the same hypothetical 120.00 price with the final deliverable value divided by 100. Then compute expiry cashflows and the break-even share price. The initial-sufficiency answer must use only memos 48921 and 49105; no later information is allowed for that answer.
All prices, premiums, positions and stress moves in this prompt are supplied hypothetical inputs, not observed historical market data. Evaluate expiry payoff only; ignore fees, taxes, financing, early exercise and other corporate actions. A local expiry-payoff sensitivity is not a pre-expiry model Greek. Amounts are USD unless stated. Return numeric amounts without intermediate rounding except where a field specifies rounding. Quote each contract term used; scenario constants need no source citation. The 2026 cutoff is an observed evidence bound, not a historical trading claim. Source memos describe different information states; respect the memo subset named by each question.

output_fields.description: Was actual final cash-in-lieu known from the initial and August 6 notices alone? Quote the August 6 disclosure; the initial notice may be additional evidence.
August 6 provisional formula evaluated at supplied S=120; do not claim an exact settlement entitlement.
Final cash component from the August 18 notice.
Total whole-share deliverable for all 50 adjusted contracts; do not divide contract count by eight.
Total fixed cash deliverable for the book.
Final deliverable market value divided by quotation multiplier; no rounding to cents.
Final minus provisional equivalent quote at the same supplied S=120, without intermediate rounding.
Aggregate strike payment if all calls exercised; strike quote remains unchanged.
Aggregate nonnegative intrinsic less original premium paid.
Exact GE price giving zero expiry P&L, to at least six decimals.
Local book expiry-P&L slope at supplied S=120 while remaining in the money, fixed cash held constant.
